availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Compact the conversation now (summarize history to free up the context window).

availableCommands.name: schedule

availableCommands.name: browser
availableCommands.description: Invoke a browser agent for web tasks.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: Plan carefully before executing a task.

availableCommands.name: grill-me
availableCommands.description: Interview me to align on a plan.

availableCommands.name: teamwork
availableCommands.description: Invoke a team of agents to autonomously tackle large projects.

availableCommands.name: learn
availableCommands.description: Reflect on recent successes or corrections to capture reusable skills or rules.

availableCommands.name: boost
availableCommands.description: Invoke the Boost multi-agent orchestrator for complex tasks.

availableCommands.name: a11y-debugging
availableCommands.description: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for accessibility (a11y) debugging and auditing based on web.dev guidelines. Use when testing semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard navigation, tap targets, and color contrast.

availableCommands.name: agy-customizations
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive guide and reference for the Antigravity Customization System. Use to explain how customizations work, their loading priority, discovery mechanisms, and to guide the creation of skills, rules, plugins, hooks, and MCP servers.

availableCommands.name: antigravity-guide
availableCommands.description: Provides a comprehensive guide, quick reference, and sitemap for Google Antigravity (AGY), including the Antigravity CLI (agy), Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity IDE, Python SDK, slash commands, keybindings, and customizations (skills, rules, MCP, sidecars). Activate this skill when the user asks questions about how to use, configure, or customize Antigravity, AGY, the agy CLI, the Antigravity IDE, or Antigravity 2.0.

availableCommands.name: chrome-devtools
availableCommands.description: Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests. This skill does not apply to `--slim` mode (MCP configuration).

availableCommands.name: code-review-and-quality
availableCommands.description: Conducts multi-axis code review. Use before merging any change. Use when reviewing code written by yourself, another agent, or a human. Use when you need to assess code quality across multiple dimensions before it enters the main branch.

availableCommands.name: context-engineering
availableCommands.description: Optimizes agent context setup. Use when starting a new session, when agent output quality degrades, when switching between tasks, or when you need to configure rules files and context for a project.

availableCommands.name: cookie-debugging
availableCommands.description: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for inspecting, debugging, and testing cookies, session state, authentication issues, and cookie consent compliance. Use when diagnosing 401/403 errors, authentication redirects, session expiration, Cookie/Set-Cookie header issues, cookie banner consent conformance, or third-party cookie/SameSite/Partitioned cookie warnings.

availableCommands.name: debug-optimize-lcp
availableCommands.description: Guides debugging and optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) using Chrome DevTools MCP tools. Use this skill whenever the user asks about LCP performance, slow page loads, Core Web Vitals optimization, or wants to understand why their page's main content takes too long to appear. Also use when the user mentions "largest contentful paint", "page load speed", "CWV", or wants to improve how fast their hero image or main content renders.

availableCommands.name: debugging-and-error-recovery
availableCommands.description: Guides systematic root-cause debugging. Use when tests fail, builds break, behavior doesn't match expectations, or you encounter any unexpected error. Use when you need a systematic approach to finding and fixing the root cause rather than guessing.

availableCommands.name: diagnosing-bugs
availableCommands.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

availableCommands.name: incremental-implementation
availableCommands.description: Delivers changes incrementally. Use when implementing any feature or change that touches more than one file. Use when you're about to write a large amount of code at once, or when a task feels too big to land in one step.

availableCommands.name: memory-leak-debugging
availableCommands.description: Diagnoses and resolves memory leaks in JavaScript/Node.js applications. Use when a user reports high memory usage, OOM errors, or wants to capture, compare, or inspect heap snapshots with Chrome DevTools MCP memory tools.

availableCommands.name: run-workflow
availableCommands.description: How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

availableCommands.name: source-driven-development
availableCommands.description: Grounds every implementation decision in official documentation. Use when you want authoritative, source-cited code free from outdated patterns. Use when building with any framework or library where correctness matters.

availableCommands.name: sub-agents
availableCommands.description: Run agent definitions as sub-agents. Use when the user names an agent or sub-agent to run, references an agent definition, or delegates a task to an agent.

availableCommands.name: swarm
availableCommands.description: (Preview & Quota Heavy) Run a swarm: several agents working in parallel on one task, each in its own conversation, collaborating through a shared message board. Use when the work splits into pieces that can be done at the same time, or when a second pair of eyes should check the first pair's work.

availableCommands.name: test-driven-development
availableCommands.description: Drives development with tests. Use when implementing any logic, fixing any bug, or changing any behavior. Use when you need to prove that code works, when a bug report arrives, or when you're about to modify existing functionality.

availableCommands.name: troubleshooting
availableCommands.description: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP and documentation to troubleshoot connection and target issues. Trigger this skill when list_pages, new_page, or navigate_page fail, or when the server initialization fails.

availableCommands.name: vercel-react-best-practices
availableCommands.description: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering. This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.

availableCommands.name: web-design-guidelines
availableCommands.description: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance. Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices".
